scopeNote.en: The special auxiliary subdivisions -1/-9, .01/.09 and `0/`9 are limited in their scope, and each series is used to denote recurrent concepts in that part of the main and common auxiliary tables for which it is designed and scheduled, or in certain other sections where specifically indicated. Thus, unlike the common auxiliary signs and subdivisions, in the special auxiliaries the same notation may be used with different meanings in different parts of the main tables, e.g. special auxiliaries -3 appear at 54, 62 and 82; special auxiliaries .02 appear at 06, 334, 53, 54, 57, 621.3, 629, 656, 66, 677, and 7. It always, however, denotes the same recurrent concept at the main number where it is listed or at the subdivisions of that number

applicationNote.en: A. Three kinds of notation are in use as special auxiliary subdivisions. (a) The hyphen series -1/-9 (but not -0, see Table 1k) are mainly analytical or differentiative in function, serving to indicate elements, components, properties and other details of the subject denoted by the main number to which they apply. Examples: the series listed at 62-1/-9, applicable (with minor exceptions) throughout 62/69, denoting engineering, mechanical and processing details; the series 82-1/-9, applicable throughout 82, denoting literary form (poetry, drama, novels, etc.). (b) The point-nought series .01/.09 are more diversely used and often developed in much more detail than -1/-9, providing sets and subsets of recurrent concepts such as aspect studies, activities, processes, operations, plant and equipment. Examples: 3.07/.08, applicable throughout 30/39 and developed in fuller detail under 35; 7.01/.09, applicable (with minor exceptions) throughout 71/79; series at many two-digit and lower-level divisions of Class 5 (e.g. 528, 53, 54, 556, 57/59), Class 8 and Class 9; and numerous series in the divisions of Class 6. (c) The apostrophe series `0/`9 are usually more specific than -1/-9 and .01/.09, and are often synthetic or integrative in function, denoting compound subjects by compound notation. They are sometimes fully listed, but elsewhere are derived from main numbers by parallel division. Examples: Synthesis of subdivisions of 329 'Political parties', e.g. 329.17`23`12 Nationalist-republican-liberal parties (from 329.17, 329.23 and 329.12). Specification of compounds at 547 'Organic chemistry' by `11/`19 (derived from 546.1/.9) and `2/`8 (derived from 547.2/.8), e.g. 547.426.24`171 Nitroglycerine (from 546.17). Specification of alloys at 669 'Metallurgy', e.g. 669.35`5`6 Copper-zinc-tin alloys (from 669.35, 669.5 and 669.6). Listed apostrophe auxiliaries, as at 628.1`1 'Characteristics of waterworks systems', 81`0 'Phases of development of languages', 81`2/`44 'Subject fields of linguistics' and 903`1 'Prehistoric culture forms'. B. Special auxiliaries may be used either single or in combination with other auxiliaries. (a) Citing a single auxiliary, e.g. 329.052 Opposition parties. 329.12`23 Liberal-republican parties. 547.29-41 Reagents for organic acids. 547.29.07 Preparation of organic acids. 547.29`26 Acid-alcohol esters. 821.161.1-31 Russian novels. 821.161.1.09 Criticism of Russian literature. (b) Citing several auxiliaries with the same symbol (a homogeneous chain), e.g. 329.053.052 Opposition splinter parties. 329.12`13`23 Liberal-progressive-republican parties. 62-242-436 Engine pistons - spherical. 678.6.067.029.4 Polycondensate mouldings - joining. (c) Citing several auxiliaries with different symbols (a heterogeneous chain), e.g. 329.12`23.052 Liberal-republican opposition parties. 547.29`26.07-41 Acid-alcohol ester preparation - reagents. 821.161.1-31.09 Russian novels - criticism
